clue.text: Bound to return grand, do so after customs search?

indicators.note: to return asks for the word for bound to be read from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: to bound is to caper, leap about
K stands for a thousand, which slang calls a grand

explanation.surface: A traveller hurries to put things back in the case after customs have rifled through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' signals the turnaround. The definition is a whole phrase: once customs officers have searched a bag, you must pack it again.
explanation.definitionFit: Packing a case again is exactly the job left once customs officers have emptied it out.

clue.text: One moving home's new free housing great, with roof missing

indicators.note: housing means the rearranged letters contain the other piece
new means the letters of free are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry the roof is the top letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: huge means great, very big

explanation.surface: A refugee's new house is huge and free but lacks a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals the anagram, 'housing' the container, and 'with roof missing' the loss of the top letter, since in a down entry the first letter is the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A refugee is someone forced to flee their home and move elsewhere for safety.

clue.text: See 7
Describing old tea only brewed in Leicester, say, less hot

indicators.note: in says the brewed letters go inside the other piece
less takes the letter for hot out of the cheese

parts.note: Red Leicester is a British cheese, so Leicester is an example of cheese
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: brewed suggests the word only is stewed up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tea served in the city of Leicester, made without heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' signals the anagram, 'less' the deletion and 'in' the container. Ceylon was the old name of Sri Lanka; Red Leicester is an English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceylonese means of Ceylon, the former name of Sri Lanka, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Hence 5 request

parts.note: so can mean hence, therefore
the answer to 5 down is legal, and licit means legal

explanation.surface: A bare cross-reference: therefore, a lawful request.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 points to 5 down, whose first word is LEGAL; LICIT is a synonym of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for or petition for something, a synonym of request as a verb.

clue.text: I'm still deciding to support backbone

indicators.note: to support in a down entry means the hesitation sits below the word for back, holding it up

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
um is the noise someone makes while still deciding

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates, still deciding whether to back an idea of spinal support.
explanation.walkthrough: The solver must read 'backbone' as two words, 'back' and 'bone', though it is printed as one. 'to support' places one piece under the other in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The sternum is the flat breastbone at the front of the chest.

clue.text: Lawyer on beer: lager not entirely wasted

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket
ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: wasted suggests the remaining letters are wrecked into a new order
not entirely means the word lager loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A lawyer drinks beer and gets half drunk on lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims the last letter and 'wasted' signals the anagram. In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, a standard crossword source of LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal eagle is an informal term for a sharp, clever lawyer.

clue.text: See 20
Something concentrated on river in book

indicators.note: in says the other pieces go inside the word for book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
atop means on top of
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A concentrated sauce described as a river within a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, a favourite crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato purée is a thick paste of tomatoes reduced down, a concentrated form.

clue.text: Go over shortly, as something thrown

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, its last letter dropped

parts.note: to discuss a matter is to go over it

explanation.surface: A topic quickly reviewed, like something hurled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts the last S from DISCUSS; 'as' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is the heavy disc thrown by athletes in field events.

clue.text: Over fifty? Wrong!

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters before it are put the wrong way round, mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone guesses an age above fifty and is told they are mistaken.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of OVER FIFTY, signalled by 'Wrong', is the number, which is indeed not over fifty, so the whole clue is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty-five falls short of fifty, so calling it over fifty would be wrong, which is the whole joke.

clue.text: Train, one behind his partner?

definitions.meaning: to train or prepare someone for a role, as a candidate is readied for office
a bridegroom, whose partner the bride walks ahead of him in a sense; the question mark flags the playful definition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' here is a verb, not a railway; the second definition is a jokey description of a husband-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: Groom means both to coach for a role and the man getting married to his bride.

clue.text: Heavy metal fan composer's knocked over, given oxygen

indicators.note: knocked over suggests the composer's name is toppled, its letters read backwards

parts.note: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer; the 's joins him to the verb
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A rock fan topples a composer's bust and is then given oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' signals the turnaround; 'given' is the link. Grebo is a dated British term, so the composer is the easier way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Grebo is British slang for a long-haired fan of heavy metal or grunge rock.

clue.text: Vessel morphing to a lab vessel

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel

indicators.note: morphing means changing shape, so the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A container changes shape into a piece of laboratory glassware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'morphing' signals the anagram. The setter uses 'vessel' twice in two senses: first a container, then the definition, a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal boat is a narrow craft for inland waterways, a vessel in the shipping sense.

clue.text: See 17
Hero's left leaving Capulet or, WS's writings suggested, his departure tempered melancholia?

indicators.note: suggested means the letters gathered are rearranged to hint at a new phrase

parts.note: taken as written, with the S of the possessive as a letter

indicators.note: leaving means the letter for left departs from the name Capulet

parts.note: WS for William Shakespeare, with the possessive S as a letter

explanation.surface: Romeo the hero departs from the Capulet house, and Shakespeare's lines say his leaving softened grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes L out of CAPULET; 'suggested' rearranges HEROS, CAPUET, OR, WSS and WRITINGS into Juliet's line from Romeo and Juliet, said at the balcony.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's line says saying goodbye is a bittersweet sorrow, grief softened by sweetness at Romeo's leaving.

clue.text: Producing square eggs, might you lose?

definitions.meaning: laying eggs badly, as a hen producing square ones would be laying wrongly
to lose something by putting it down and forgetting where

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the word as MIS (badly) plus LAY (produce eggs); 'might you' is padding that joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislay is to put something somewhere and forget it, effectively to lose it for a while.

clue.text: See 14
E, say, on this for the trip of a lifetime once?

definitions.text: this for the trip of a lifetime once

parts.note: E stands for east, and the Orient is the East
to say something is to express it

explanation.surface: A sign reading E, say, on the famous train for a once-in-a-lifetime journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces. The definition refers to the luxury train from Paris to Istanbul, once a byword for a grand journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous luxury train from Paris to Constantinople made journeys that passengers treated as a once-in-a-lifetime trip.

clue.text: Story written up about old soldier

indicators.note: about means the reversed word goes around the other piece
written up in a down entry means the word is set upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: a report is a story in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A journalist writes up a story about an old soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written up' turns REPORT into TROPER, and 'about' puts it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier, especially in a cavalry or armoured unit.

clue.text: What toothless parrot might have to do when talking to do well

indicators.note: when talking says the phrase before it is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.words: What toothless parrot might have to do
parts.note: a bird with no teeth cannot crack its seed, so it would have to suck seed instead

explanation.surface: A parrot without teeth must suck its food, a picture of feeble achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when talking' signals a sound-alike: SUCK SEED said out loud is the word for doing well; parrots are, of course, talkers.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed is to achieve what you set out to do, to do well.

clue.text: See 14

parts.note: the cross-reference gives Juliet's line about parting, read as a lethal sweet treat: the parting is a death, the sweetness a rich confection

explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads PARTING (dying) IS SUCH SWEET... as a way of dying from sweet things, the name of a famously rich dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: The rich cake's name jokes that it is so sweet it would kill you, a fatal parting through sweetness.

clue.text: Run school division

definitions.meaning: a run is a small flowing body of water, a brook
a set or band into which pupils of similar ability are grouped

explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' is a noun for a brook, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a flowing brook and also a British school's ability group.

clue.text: Standard 21, as may be pronounced?

indicators.note: as may be pronounced says the word for 21 is meant to be heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the answer to 21 down is stream, and a trickler is a playful word for a small stream, something that trickles

explanation.surface: A cross-referenced clue asking whether a standard can be spoken another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is STREAM; a TRICKLER is one, and said out loud it is close to the flag's name. The question mark admits the sound-alike is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and a tricolour is a flag of three bands such as the French one.

clue.text: Orders last of cake — though evidently shouldn't?

definitions.text: Orders last of cake — though evidently shouldn't?

parts.note: OBEs are awards of the Order of the British Empire, so the plural means orders

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of the word cake is taken

explanation.surface: Someone orders the last slice of cake even though they plainly ought not to.
explanation.walkthrough: OBEs plus E from 'last of cake'; the whole clue doubles as the definition, a fat person who should not order more cake.
explanation.definitionFit: An obese person is very overweight and evidently should not be ordering more cake.

clue.text: When turning, bend back bones

indicators.note: turning means the word for when is read backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I arrived

indicators.note: back asks for the word for bend to be read in reverse

parts.note: an arc is a bend or curve

explanation.surface: Someone turns and bends their back, aching in the bones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes SA from AS and 'back' makes CRA from ARC.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacra is the plural of sacrum, the triangular bone at the base of the spine.

clue.text: Top a ton, one of four if human?

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, and C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
humans have four limbs: two arms and two legs

explanation.surface: Someone hitting a hundred gets to the top, as a human might on all fours.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'a ton' is a hundred. 'Top' is a verb: to get to the top of.
explanation.definitionFit: To top a hill is to climb it all the way to the summit.

clue.text: See 5
Quite unfortunate about the gutlessly self-important

indicators.note: about means the piece for quite unfortunate goes around the other piece

parts.note: poorish means rather poor, somewhat unfortunate

indicators.note: gutlessly means the word the loses its middle, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A rather unlucky remark about a cowardly, pompous person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutlessly' leaves the outer letters and 'about' signals the container. Mr Pooter is the pompous clerk of the comic novel The Diary of a Nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooterish describes a pompous petty self-importance, after Charles Pooter in The Diary of a Nobody.

clue.text: Man manipulating the whole currency, nothing less

parts.note: the mass is the whole or the bulk of something

indicators.note: less says a piece is taken away from the word for currency

parts.note: the euro is the currency of much of Europe
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man juggles all the money, nothing less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' signals the deletion, with nothing as O. The definition is a man whose work is manipulating muscles, not a schemer.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur is a man whose job is massage, manipulating the body's muscles.

clue.text: Small and plump, short and 23

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothes labels
tubby means plump, rounded

explanation.surface: A description of someone small and plump.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is OBESE, so the definition reads 'short and obese'; 'and' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubby means short and thick, squat, which matches short and fat.
